name: Becton, Dickinson and Company
executive_summary: Becton, Dickinson (BDX) is a global medtech franchise spanning medication delivery, connected care, biopharma systems and interventional products, now simplified after the February 2026 combination of its Biosciences & Diagnostic Solutions unit with Waters Corporation. The quantitative screen flags the name as a buy on cheapness (FCF yield ~10.5%), quality (Piotroski F-Score 8/9) and financial health, despite a depressed 6.7% ROE and P/E of 27.2x. The valuation hook is a sharp share-price drawdown (roughly 23–30% year-to-date per news coverage) against what appears to be durable cash generation and a balance sheet being actively de-levered with ~$4bn of divestiture proceeds. The central debate is whether post-portfolio-remediation earnings power and simplification benefits will outweigh heavy litigation reserves (~$1.7bn), multiple FDA quality actions, and one-off restructuring charges that distorted the most recent quarter. Deep research partially confirms the screen’s cash-flow case but flags material non-financial risks the quant models under-weight.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, BDX offers a classic “quality at a discount” setup: a wide-moat, consumables-heavy medtech platform trading below recent highs with screen metrics that align on cash, not headline P/E alone. The screen passes FCF Yield, Piotroski F-Score (8/9), Composite Value, Earnings Quality and Financial Health across 20/20 data points with high data quality — a rare full metric set. FCF yield of ~10.5% and dividend yield of 2.8% provide an income and capital-return floor; the board authorised a further 10 million-share repurchase programme in January 2026 and executed ~$2bn of accelerated buybacks using Waters proceeds.

Business quality supports the cheapness signal: recurring razor/blade economics in infusion, specimen management and interventional portfolios; global scale (~72,000 associates, 61 countries per FY2025 10-K); and strategic focus on higher-growth connected care after shedding lower-return Life Sciences assets. The Edwards Critical Care acquisition (closed September 2024 for ~$3.9bn) adds hemodynamic monitoring to Connected Care, though purchase-accounting amortisation continues to suppress reported earnings. Post-Waters, continuing operations grew H1 FY2026 revenues 4.4% year-on-year to $9.2bn (10-Q, six months ended 31 March 2026), suggesting underlying demand remains intact despite market pessimism. Tangible book is deeply negative given ~$36bn of goodwill and intangibles — typical for acquisitive medtech — which partly explains the low ROE and argues for FCF-based rather than book-based valuation, consistent with the screen’s emphasis on FCF yield over P/B alone (1.8x).
financial_review:
**Annual filings (gap noted).** The FY2025 10-K (filed 25 November 2025) and FY2024 10-K (filed 27 November 2024) are indexed with body extracts available, but those extracts are truncated at 80,000 characters and contain business description and risk factors only — consolidated income statements, balance sheets and cash-flow statements are not present in the downloaded bodies. Annual figures below therefore fall back to `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo), stated explicitly.

| Metric (Yahoo fallback, FY ended 30 Sep) | FY2025 | FY2024 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | $21.84bn | $20.18bn | +8.2% |
| Operating income | $2.99bn | $2.86bn | +4.5% |
| Net income | $1.68bn | $1.71bn | −1.6% |
| Diluted EPS | $5.82 | $5.93 | −1.9% |
| Operating cash flow | $3.43bn | $3.80bn | −9.7% |
| Free cash flow | $2.67bn | $3.07bn | −13.0% |
| Total debt | $19.18bn | $20.11bn | −4.6% |
| Net debt | $18.54bn | $18.39bn | +0.8% |

FY2025 revenue growth was aided by the Advanced Patient Monitoring acquisition; reported net income and FCF declined modestly, reflecting restructuring charges, higher interest expense ($613m vs $528m) and working-capital absorption. Normalised income (Yahoo) of ~$2.09bn versus reported $1.68bn suggests significant non-recurring drag — a pattern that intensified in FY2026.

**Interim filings (primary source — SEC 10-Q bodies).**

*Q1 FY2026 (three months ended 31 December 2025, 10-Q filed 9 February 2026):* Revenues $5.25bn (+1.6% vs $5.17bn); operating income $552m (+22%); net income $382m (+26%); diluted EPS $1.34. Pre-divestiture presentation; continuing/discontinued split not yet applied in this filing’s headline income statement.

*Q2 FY2026 (three months ended 31 March 2026, 10-Q filed 7 May 2026):* This quarter reflects the Waters transaction (completed 9 February 2026) and segment reorganisation.

| Metric | Q2 FY2026 | Q2 FY2025 | H1 FY2026 | H1 FY2025 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Continuing revenues | $4.71bn | $4.48bn | $9.20bn | $8.81bn |
| Continuing operating income | $93m | $383m | $562m | $665m |
| Continuing net income | ($37m) | $158m | $274m | $304m |
| Reported net income | ($311m) | $308m | $72m | $611m |
| Diluted EPS (reported) | ($1.11) | $1.07 | $0.25 | $2.12 |

Q2 FY2026 continuing operating income collapsed due to $533m of integration, restructuring and transaction expense (including a $450m asset impairment tied to the “Excellence Unleashed” simplification programme) versus $93m in the prior-year quarter. Discontinued operations contributed a ($274m) net loss in Q2 as Life Sciences results through the transaction date and separation costs were recognised. On a cleaner basis, segment operating income from continuing operations totalled $1.72bn in Q2 (+2% on revenue growth to $4.71bn), indicating underlying margin resilience before corporate unallocated charges.

*Balance sheet (31 March 2026 vs 30 September 2025, Q2 FY2026 10-Q):* Total assets $50.8bn (from $55.3bn post-divestiture); total debt $17.3bn ($14.7bn long-term + $2.6bn current, down from ~$19.2bn); cash and equivalents $813m; employee benefit obligations $1.03bn; shareholders’ equity $24.1bn. The company received a ~$3.86bn net cash distribution from the Waters RMT, deployed $2bn to debt tender/repayment and $2bn to accelerated share repurchases.

*Cash flow (H1 FY2026, continuing operations):* Operating cash flow $1.33bn (vs $489m H1 FY2025); capex ($233m); implying H1 FCF of roughly $1.1bn, a sharp improvement on the prior-year half despite depressed reported earnings — supportive of the screen’s FCF yield signal on a continuing-operations basis.

*Prior-year interim trend (pre-divestiture, consolidated):* Nine months ended 30 June 2025 revenues $15.95bn (+8.2% vs $14.74bn); net income $1.19bn (−9.2%); nine-month diluted EPS $4.10. Q3 FY2025 (June quarter) revenues $5.51bn (+10.4%) with net income $574m, showing momentum before FY2026 transition costs accelerated.

**Liquidity and covenants.** No going-concern language was identified in available filing bodies. The 10-K discusses elevated leverage following the Edwards acquisition and notes debt funded via commercial paper and bond issuances; Q2 FY2026 10-Q confirms active debt retirement via tender offers (8-K, 25 February 2026). Pension settlement losses of $25m were recorded in Q2 FY2026 upon plan curtailments linked to the transaction.
risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and quality.** BDX operates under an amended FDA consent decree on Alaris infusion pumps (originally 2007, inherited via CareFusion 2015), with ongoing Form 483 observations and potential penalties up to $15m per year. A separate Dispensing Warning Letter (BD Pyxis, November 2024) carries a recorded liability of $68m as of 31 March 2026, with management noting the ultimate cost could exceed accruals. A new El Paso Warning Letter (April 2026) on ChloraPrep/PurPrep combination products led to a voluntary U.S. ship hold; BD states a loss is probable but cannot yet estimate the range. Ethylene oxide sterilisation faces tightening EPA NESHAP rules and ~430 personal-injury suits near Covington, Georgia facilities (first trial: $20m compensatory award; punitive phase mistrial).

**Litigation.** Product-liability accruals totalled ~$1.7bn at 31 March 2026 ($1.8bn at 30 September 2025), covering ~6,995 hernia mesh claims, ~3,250 implantable port claims, pelvic mesh and IVC filter actions. The 10-Q states charges could exceed accruals and insurance coverage. Department of Justice False Claims Act investigations into CareFusion Alaris/Pyxis and Genesis container contracts remain active.

**Financial structure.** Despite de-leveraging, ~$17bn of debt and negative tangible book (−$10.6bn per Yahoo FY2025) constrain ROE and increase sensitivity to rates (10-year Treasury ~4.7% per macro context). FY2025 10-K risk factors flag tariff headwinds for FY2026 with limited mitigation visibility.

**Operational and governance.** CFO transition announced October 2025; executive retirement noted July 2026. Q2 FY2026’s $450m impairment and $533m restructuring charge signal portfolio rationalisation pain ahead of earnings normalisation. Government research-funding reductions flagged in FY2025 10-K may pressure Life Sciences customers (now largely divested) but also broader research-tooling demand.

**Quant screen blind spots.** Low ROE (6.7%), elevated P/E (27.2x on trailing reported earnings), and earnings-quality concerns from recurring special charges are not captured by the FCF and F-Score passes. Timing signal is “insufficient_data” on the screen itself.

research_rationale: Deep research confirms the screen’s FCF-yield and balance-sheet quality case on continuing operations, but litigation, FDA actions and transition charges warrant a measured accumulate rather than full conviction on the quantitative buy signal alone.
